name: spec-truth
body: The target-truth content of a durable spec statement: what is, or what needs to become true. Durable spec wording states a truth that holds at every moment — time-relative wording that ages (`today`, `now`, `currently`, `no longer`, `was`, `previously`) is a blocked form, because a statement true only at one moment is either the target truth or it belongs in git history, and a reviewer treats such wording as blocking history content whose fix is to rewrite it as what is. A replaced statement is updated or removed, never annotated; a `note` deepens the understanding of what is and never records the past or another note — a `note` details only the non-note node or code it deepens, and the binary refuses a `Note`→`Note` `details` edge at write time. Materializing a source spec or reconciling to an implementation rewrites the nodes to what is and leaves no provenance trail — git history, not the spec, describes the past.
